diagnosis: Schematic of the telomere and functions of the proteins affected in telomere biology disorders
legend: Protein function and reported consequences of variants in the respective gene are summarized in <<38694>>Table 6.01. Components are grouped approximately based on their function. The components of the telomerase enzyme complex (DKC1, TERC, TERT, NAF1, NOP10, NHP2), telomerase or TERC regulators (TCAB1, PARN, and ZCHC8), and RTEL1 are shown in green. Dark blue indicates the shelterin (TPP1, TIN2, and POT1) and the CST (CST1 and STN1) complexes. Proteins primarily involved in DNA repair are shown in red. The red line indicates that Apollo interacts with TRF2. NPM1 is involved in ribosomal RNA maturation, and interacts with NAF1 and NHP2. MDM4 is not shown because it does not directly act at the telomere. Grey symbols indicate known key telomere biology proteins not yet attributed to human disease (GAR1 in the telomerase complex; TRF1, TRF2, RAP1 in shelterin; and TEN1 in the CST complex). Yellow asterisk – autosomal dominant; light blue asterisk – autosomal recessive; orange asterisk – X-linked recessive.

aAll listed gene variants can occur de novo, but this is frequently reported in TINF2. bSomatic reversion of mutations in blood-derived DNA has been reported. cSkewed X chromosome inactivation may result in phenotypically affected females. dTBD-associated variants in MDM4 were first discovered in the NCI cohort but the patients were not included owing to the inclusion criteria of Niewisch et al. {31478401;34852175}. eUSB1 is only listed because some phenotypes overlap, but the reported patients’ phenotypes are more consisted with PN and/or RTS.

Note: Germline pathogenic variants in these genes have been reported in patients with classic DC and/or those with overlapping medical problems without the classic mucocutaneous triad, hence the TBD designation. The approximate frequency of TBDs is estimated based on reports in the literature and the author’s experience; it is not intended to be quantitative because of ascertainment biases of the different published studies. The approximate frequency for common is 10–20%, for rare < 10%, and very rare < 1%.
